verdict: Red 8/10 REJECT, blue 7/10 PARTIALLY OVERTURNED - but overturned on severity tags only; the recommendation and the core case are SUSTAINED, so the benches are not discordant. The decisive finding is that the thesis's entire reason for being - a two-engines dispersion in which a $36.7B agency servicing franchise is credit-insensitive and therefore damage-absent - is refuted by the Q2'26 10-Q. Arbor retains Fannie Mae DUS loss-sharing on that book: the loss-sharing allowance ran $97.6M to $118.9M, the guarantee obligation is $36.6M, and $18.0M of provision was already taken in H1'26. Both engines are long the same 2021-vintage multifamily credit. Blue sustained that fact and correctly cut the inference from FATAL to SIZING: the allowance is ~0.32% of the $36.7B portfolio and the ~$36M/yr provision run-rate sits against ~$195M/yr of servicing and escrow revenue, so the agency engine is damaged, not worthless - the dispersion is smaller, not zero. Blue's second and more useful correction is to red's book-convergence kill. Red argued the $375M of 6.25% converts struck at ~$6.10 (164.0016 shares per $1,000) put a 29% dilution wall overhead that collapses book convergence above the strike. The arithmetic is right, the inference is not: full conversion adds 61.5M shares AT $6.10, giving pro-forma book per share of roughly (209M x $11.59 + $375M) / 270.5M, or about $10.34. Upside decelerates above the strike, it does not cap - this is the same over-tagging artifact blue benches keep catching. What survives after both reductions is still decisive and still negative: a $0.17 dividend paid on $0.10 of distributable earnings with $20-30M/qtr of realized losses guided, so the next dated event is a probable second cut and longs are paid to wait into a negative catalyst; a 1.35% allowance ($163.4M) against a $12.11B book with ~$1.07B of NPAs, i.e. ~15% NPA coverage, where guided realized losses consume the entire allowance in about six quarters - so either reserves rise and book falls, or book is overstated, and $10.95 is not conservatively marked either way; and an open, unquantified left tail in the DOJ/FBI inquiry and E.D.N.Y. class action, confirmed 2024-vintage with no 2026 resolution found. Blue's timing correction matters for pack construction: there is no dated pre-Q3 cut event - the cut decision lands AT the ~Oct-30 print, and the current dividend has a 8/14 record and 8/28 pay date. Critically, this fails the dislocation test outright. No forced seller and no mechanism is named; ~29% of float is short (Mar-2026, stale) and coverage is heavy, so this is a crowded, cause-identified battleground - consensus repricing, not dislocation. Blue applied the conditioning doctrine correctly: a 29% short base is squeeze fuel, which is a reason not to be short, not a reason to be long. RP_FAIR does not bind - fairness is not verified and the litigation tail is unbounded. Blue's one genuine pro-long finding, which red never engaged, is that the July convert placement is itself a market-clearing refutation of the terminal-funding narrative - $375M of unsecured three-year money placed, though at a 6.25% cash coupon that says access is intact but expensive. That is a reason the name is not a zero, not a reason to own it.
